display_name: Howard Park Leston Shiraz, Margaret River
raw_content:
{
  "hook": "Ironstone pebbles in the Leston vineyard force the vines to struggle; the 2016 Shiraz that results is Margaret River in a cool, pepper-spiced key, not the usual chocolate-rich one.",
  "wine_summary": "Howard Park was among the first to plant Shiraz on the ridge that runs north-south through Wilyabrup; the Leston block sits on lateritic ironstone gravel that drains fast and holds little nitrogen, so the vines stay small-cropped and the berries stay thick-skinned. Those skins give the wine its black-tea tannin and cracked-pepper top-notes, the sort of detail that wins bronze at TEXSOM while bigger, sweeter styles miss the podium. Margaret River’s maritime diurnal swing (16 °C night-day drop in March) keeps acidity high even at 14% alcohol, so the wine reads medium-bodied, not hedonistic.",
  "terroir_expression": "Red gravelly loam shot through with ironstone buckshot stores less water than the region’s deeper loams; the vines shut down early, concentrating pyrazines (that green-peppercorn note) and cassis skin tannins. Afternoon sea breeze off Geographe Bay lowers mean daily temp by 2 °C versus the valley floor, stretching hang-time and locking in a pH that lets malolactic finish fully without sacrificing freshness.",
  "vinification_summary": "Small-lot open-top fermenters get 20% whole bunches; carbonic maceration inside the berries softens seed tannins and adds stem-ginger spice, then the wine ages 14 months in 30% new French hogsheads. The heads are steamed, not toasted, so oak lactones stay low and vineyard pepper shows through.",
  "food_pairing": "Nashville hot chicken—alcohol and tannin absorb cayenne oil, while pyrazine pepper mirrors the spice. Kangaroo fillet with native pepperberry—game iron plus berry tannin echo the wine’s own structure. Eggplant and miso kasu vegetarian ramen—umami replaces meat, high acid cuts through miso fat. 12-hour Texas-style brisket—smoke and black-tea tannin share phenolic family tree. Aged cheddar (24-month)—salt crystals pull out fruit, while acid scrubs butterfat.",
  "comparable_wines": "Xanadu DJL Shiraz 2016 — same iron-gravel ridge, more dark-fruit drive, less pepper. Leeuwin Art Series Shiraz 2015 — warmer vineyard, darker chocolate profile, silkier tannin. Henschke ‘Henry’s Seven’ Barossa 2018 — Rhône-blend, shares pepper but adds raspberry compote.",
  "style_profile": "Medium-full dry red with ironstone-etched tannins and cracked-pepper lift",
  "cellar_recommendation": "Drink 2024-2028 to keep the pepper edge; if you like leather development, hold to 2030 but don’t cellar past 12 years total. 55°F/13°C constant, no need to decant unless reductive funk shows.",
  "value_assessment": "A$35-40 retail in Australia, US$32-38 ex-tax. Competes head-on with Wirra Wirra ‘Woodhenge’ Shiraz at A similar price; Leston offers more site-specific pepper and less oak gloss. Worth the ask if you want Margaret River structure without the usual $60+ tariff.",
  "market_position": "You’ll spot it by-the-glass at Melbourne wine bars pushing regional variety over ripeness; independents stock it for collectors who know Howard Park’s 90s track record but won’t pay ‘Abercrombie’ money. Exports mainly to Canada and the U.K., less to the U.S.—good hunting on import lists.",
  "insider_take": "Most drinkers expect Margaret River Shiraz to taste like blackberry pie; this one flips the script toward northern Rhône pepper and iron. If you crave plush fruit, buy the 2015 instead—2016 is for the acid-heads. And ignore the bronze medals—they signal restraint, not mediocrity.",

parsed.wine_summary: Howard Park was among the first to plant Shiraz on the ridge that runs north-south through Wilyabrup; the Leston block sits on lateritic ironstone gravel that drains fast and holds little nitrogen, so the vines stay small-cropped and the berries stay thick-skinned. Those skins give the wine its black-tea tannin and cracked-pepper top-notes, the sort of detail that wins bronze at TEXSOM while bigger, sweeter styles miss the podium. Margaret River’s maritime diurnal swing (16 °C night-day drop in March) keeps acidity high even at 14% alcohol, so the wine reads medium-bodied, not hedonistic.
parsed.terroir_expression: Red gravelly loam shot through with ironstone buckshot stores less water than the region’s deeper loams; the vines shut down early, concentrating pyrazines (that green-peppercorn note) and cassis skin tannins. Afternoon sea breeze off Geographe Bay lowers mean daily temp by 2 °C versus the valley floor, stretching hang-time and locking in a pH that lets malolactic finish fully without sacrificing freshness.
parsed.vinification_summary: Small-lot open-top fermenters get 20% whole bunches; carbonic maceration inside the berries softens seed tannins and adds stem-ginger spice, then the wine ages 14 months in 30% new French hogsheads. The heads are steamed, not toasted, so oak lactones stay low and vineyard pepper shows through.

parsed.market_position: You’ll spot it by-the-glass at Melbourne wine bars pushing regional variety over ripeness; independents stock it for collectors who know Howard Park’s 90s track record but won’t pay ‘Abercrombie’ money. parsed.insider_take: Most drinkers expect Margaret River Shiraz to taste like blackberry pie; this one flips the script toward northern Rhône pepper and iron. If you crave plush fruit, buy the 2015 instead—2016 is for the acid-heads. And ignore the bronze medals—they signal restraint, not mediocrity.
